core_obligations: Reduce the vanishing of R^p j_*F to a stalk computation and use that formation of higher direct images commutes with flat base change, so that one may assume X is the spectrum of a Noetherian local ring of dimension at most one (proof lines 7755-7760).

In that case, list the closed point x and the finitely many points x_1, ..., x_n specializing to x but to no other point, and observe that if x lies in U then U = X so the result is clear, while otherwise U is the finite discrete set of the remaining points (proof lines 7761-7766).
Use that a finite discrete scheme is affine and conclude the vanishing of the higher direct images, completing the proof within the counted span (proof lines 7766-7770).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to stalks and apply flat base change to reach the local case.
Describe the possibilities for the quasi-compact open U in the local case.
Use affineness of the resulting pieces to conclude the vanishing.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the vanishing of the higher direct images R^p j_* F for the inclusion j of a quasi-compact open U into a scheme whose local rings are Noetherian of dimension at most one, which is the key input for the affineness criterion for such opens. The proof reduces the vanishing to a stalk computation and uses flat base change to assume that X is the spectrum of a Noetherian local ring of dimension at most one (proof lines 7755-7763). In that case X has a closed point x and finitely many other points specializing to it and to no other point, so U is either all of X or the finite set of the remaining points, which is affine; the argument then concludes the vanishing (proof lines 7764-7794). H2: the flat-base-change reduction to the local case and the resulting explicit description of U are the substance.
